correctness.rationale: Pass for the frozen theorem. On the centered space, for r>λ the derivative is (1−λ/r)I+(λ/r)uuᵀ, with u the unit centered radial direction; for r<λ it is zero. A nonconstant centered line intersects the sphere in at most two points, so piecewise integration and directional quotients as r decreases to λ identify the sharp coefficient with the maximal rank-one norm. In path differences, the norm of uuᵀ is V(u) max_j |uᵀb_j|, where b_j is a centered cut step. Writing V(u) as the maximum of (Dᵀσ)ᵀu, the rank-two Rayleigh calculation gives (||Dᵀσ||₂||b_j||₂+|(Dᵀσ)ᵀb_j|)/2. The inner product has magnitude one; alternating signs maximize the first squared norm at 4n−6 and a middle cut gives the second at floor(n²/4)/n. Their simultaneous maximizer gives the stated coefficient and a norming direction. For n≥3 every differentiable point of a nonconstant centered segment has derivative norm strictly below the coefficient; integration is strict for each finite positive-denominator pair, while perturbations by the cut step just outside the sphere approach equality. A same-sign exterior ray attains one in n=2 and at λ=0 the map is the identity. Centering and radial scaling give the one-input bound; Euclidean nonexpansivity follows from the stated convex proximal representation. Expanding the root gives n/2+1/8+O(1/n). Independent replay in branches/0941b798-12a2-427e-a36c-93ad058cfe5f/independent_finite_check.py enumerated signs and cuts through n=9 and reproduced near-sphere witnesses; those checks support the arithmetic, not the general proof.
